summary: Trace motor commands through nerves and muscles to signals useful for movement analysis and assistive control.
outcomes: Distinguish muscle activity, peripheral nerve activity and movement measurements.
Explain envelope features, crosstalk and fatigue-related interpretation limits.
sequence: Follow a motor command to a muscle contraction
Compare surface, intramuscular and nerve measurements
Assess posture, contact shift, crosstalk and fatigue

visual.question: Can the same movement produce different measured EMG?
visual.interaction: Change synthetic motor-unit recruitment, sensor mixing and contact gain.

practice.task: Classify simple actions from supplied deidentified EMG using a grouped split.
practice.success: Includes a baseline and explains signal confounds without inferring force directly from amplitude.
